headline: US stocks ended mixed on midterm Election Day as AI and chip names rebounded ahead of key earnings
raw_text:
- US indices finished mixed, with the S&P 500 ($SPX) up 0.36% to 7,568.92, the Nasdaq Composite ($COMP) up 0.83% to 25,372.01, the Russell 2000 (IWM) up 0.23% to 2,812.45, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average ($DJI) down 197 points, or 0.38%, to 51,786.72.
- Information technology climbed 1.31% and industrials rose 0.96%, while seven of 11 S&P 500 ($SPX) sectors declined, led by materials down 1.93% and consumer staples off 1.76%.
- AI-related leaders drove the tech rebound, with NVIDIA (NVDA) up about 2.3%, Microsoft (MSFT) up about 2.7%, and Amazon (AMZN) up 2.06%.
- AMD (AMD) gained about 3.7% ahead of results, then reported Q3 adjusted EPS of $2.09 versus $1.95 expected on $13.38 billion in revenue, with data-center revenue up 97% year over year to a record $8.55 billion and Q4 revenue guidance near $17 billion topping consensus, pushing shares higher after hours.
- Apple (AAPL) fell 1.9% after warning its gross margins would be pressured by rising memory chip costs.
- Super Micro Computer (SMCI) advanced about 9.5% after hours after beating expectations with record Q1 revenue of $19.9 billion, nearly quadrupling from a year earlier, delivering adjusted EPS of $1.81 versus $1.23 expected, and guiding fiscal-year sales as high as $82 billion while raising its fiscal 2027 outlook to $72–82 billion on strong AI server demand.
- Block (XYZ) beat third-quarter estimates and raised guidance, with shares up about 6.7% after hours, adding to a busy after-hours earnings slate.
- Investors prepared for final US midterm election outcomes and another wave of earnings reports tomorrow.
